subject.title: Bug: Billing error (402) causes infinite retry death spiral for inline-apiKey providers (no backoff)

question: Should OpenClaw adopt provider-level fail-closed cooldown state for inline `models.providers.<id>.apiKey` credentials, including a persisted `inline-api-key:<provider>` usage namespace, or keep billing cooldowns profile-only?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the durable cooldown identity and upgrade behavior for inline keys are auth-provider policy choices that should be accepted before the linked fix lands.

options.title: Accept provider-level cooldown
options.body: Land or rebuild the linked fix so inline keys receive the same billing/auth cooldown protection as profile-backed credentials while preserving healthy stored profiles as fallback.

options.title: Keep profile-only cooldowns
options.body: Document auth-profile migration as the supported path and close the implementation PR as not planned for inline credentials.

options.title: Request narrower design
options.body: Pause the linked PR until maintainers specify the exact cooldown identity, persistence, and recovery behavior for inline keys.

recommendation.title: Accept provider-level cooldown
recommendation.body: Land or rebuild the linked fix so inline keys receive the same billing/auth cooldown protection as profile-backed credentials while preserving healthy stored profiles as fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent auth cooldown and profile-usage history makes this the best available routing candidate for the cooldown policy decision.
